cases.sentence: ___ был прекрасный, и гонка лодок, и все это было довольно мило.
cases.translation: The dinner was excellent, and the boat race, and it was all rather nice.
cases.explain: Обед is the subject of «был» (was), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: «Ведь ты знаешь, для чего. Для тебя и для ___, которые будут», — сказал он.
cases.translation: "You know why. For you, and for the children who will come," he said.
cases.explain: The preposition для (for) governs the genitive case, giving ребёнка.

cases.sentence: «Как обыкновенно», — отвечал он, тотчас же по одному ___ на нее, поняв, что она в одном из своих хороших расположений.
cases.translation: "As usual," he answered, understanding from a single glance at her that she was in one of her good moods.
cases.explain: The preposition по (from/by) governs the dative case here, giving взгляду (a glance).
Гостей is the direct object of the transitive verb назвал (named), so it takes the accusative (identical to the genitive plural for this animate noun).

cases.sentence: — О, да, — сказал он, с ___ взглянув в ее взволнованное лицо.
cases.translation: "Oh, yes," he said, glancing at her agitated face with anxiety.
cases.explain: The preposition с (with) governs the instrumental case, giving беспокойством (anxiety).

cases.sentence: «Зачем ждать здесь развода? Разве не все равно в ___?»
cases.translation: "Why wait here for the divorce? Isn't it all the same in the country?"
cases.explain: The preposition в (in) denoting location governs the prepositional case, giving деревне.

reading.ru: «Что ж, было весело?» — спросила она, с виноватым и кротким выражением на лице, выходя к нему навстречу.
reading.question: How did Anna greet Vronsky when he returned home?
options: With a guilty, gentle expression, asking if it had been fun
reading.correct: With a guilty, gentle expression, asking if it had been fun
reading.explain: The text says she went to meet him with a guilty and gentle expression, asking whether it had been fun.

reading.ru: Вот это хорошо», — сказал он, указывая на сундуки в передней.
reading.question: What did Vronsky point to when he said "Now that's good"?
options: The trunks in the front hall
reading.correct: The trunks in the front hall
reading.explain: The text says he pointed at the trunks in the front hall, saying "Now that's good."

reading.ru: И она на мгновение почувствовала в себе поднимающееся желание борьбы, но, сделав усилие над собой, она подавила его и встретила Вронского так же весело.
reading.question: What did Anna do with her rising urge to fight after Vronsky's remark?
options: Suppressed it and greeted him just as cheerfully
reading.correct: Suppressed it and greeted him just as cheerfully
reading.explain: The text says she felt a rising desire to argue but, making an effort, suppressed it and met Vronsky just as cheerfully.

reading.ru: «Знаешь, на меня нашло почти вдохновение», — говорила она.
reading.question: How did Anna describe her sudden feeling about leaving for the country?
reading.explain: Anna says "an almost inspiration came over me" (нашло почти вдохновение).

reading.ru: Я решила, что это не будет больше иметь влияние на мою жизнь.
reading.question: What did Anna decide about the pending divorce?
options: It would no longer influence her life
She would fight for it in court
She would ask her husband for it again
She would give up on it entirely
reading.correct: It would no longer influence her life
reading.explain: Anna says she decided it would no longer have any influence on her life.

reading.ru: Явилась какая-то дама-учительница плавания шведской королевы и показывала свое искусство.
reading.question: What unusual entertainment did Vronsky describe from the dinner?
options: A female swimming instructor of the Swedish queen demonstrating her skill
reading.correct: A female swimming instructor of the Swedish queen demonstrating her skill
reading.explain: The text says a lady swimming-teacher of the Swedish queen appeared and showed off her skill.

reading.ru: «Так когда же ты думаешь ехать?» Анна встряхнула головой, как бы желая отогнать неприятную мысль.
reading.question: What did Anna do when asked when she thought of leaving?
options: Shook her head as if driving away an unpleasant thought
reading.correct: Shook her head as if driving away an unpleasant thought
reading.explain: The text says Anna shook her head as though trying to chase away an unpleasant thought.

reading.ru: Мне надо быть у маман», — сказал Вронский, смутившись.
reading.question: Why did Vronsky hesitate about leaving on Sunday?
options: He needed to visit his mother
reading.correct: He needed to visit his mother
reading.explain: Vronsky says he needs to be at his mother's ("maman") on Sunday, growing embarrassed as he says it.

reading.ru: Теперь уже не учительница шведской королевы, а княжна Сорокина, которая жила в подмосковной деревне вместе с графиней Вронской, представилась Анне.
reading.question: Who did Anna now imagine in place of the swimming teacher?
reading.explain: The text says now it was not the swimming teacher but Princess Sorokina who appeared to Anna's mind.

reading.ru: «Для тебя это не имеет смысла, потому что до меня тебе никакого дела нет.
reading.question: What did Anna accuse Vronsky of regarding sense and meaning?
options: That things made no sense to him because he did not care about her
That he never listened to her
That he was lying to her
That he wanted to leave her
reading.correct: That things made no sense to him because he did not care about her
reading.explain: Anna says it makes no sense to him because he has no business caring about her.

reading.ru: «Уважение выдумали для того, чтобы скрывать пустое место, где должна быть любовь.
reading.question: What did Anna say respect was invented to conceal?
options: An empty space where love should be
reading.correct: An empty space where love should be
reading.explain: Anna says respect was invented to hide the empty place where love ought to be.

reading.ru: «Что вы хотите этим сказать?» — вскрикнула она, с ужасом вглядываясь в явное выражение ненависти, которое было во всем лице и в особенности в жестоких грозных глазах.
reading.question: What expression on Vronsky's face horrified Anna?
options: An evident expression of hatred, especially in his cruel eyes
reading.correct: An evident expression of hatred, especially in his cruel eyes
reading.explain: The text says she gazed with horror at the plain expression of hatred on his whole face, especially his cruel, menacing eyes.

reading.ru: Нет, есть границы терпению, вскрикнул он и быстро выпустил ее руку.
reading.question: What did Vronsky exclaim as he released her hand?
options: That there are limits to patience
That he loved her more than ever
reading.correct: That there are limits to patience
reading.explain: Vronsky cries out that there are limits to patience and quickly lets go of her hand.

reading.ru: Мысли о том, куда она поедет теперь, к тетке ли, у которой она воспитывалась, к Долле, или просто одна за границу, и о том, что он делает теперь один в кабинете, окончательная ли это ссора, или, возможно, еще примирение, и о том, что теперь будут говорить про нее все ее петербургские бывшие знакомые, Как посмотрит на это Алексей Александрович, и много других мыслей о том, что будет теперь, после разрыва, приходили ей в голову, но она не всею душой отдавалась этим мыслям.
reading.question: Which of the following was NOT among the thoughts occupying Anna as she sat before the mirror?
options: Going to her aunt, to Dolly, or abroad alone
reading.explain: The text lists Anna's swirling thoughts—her aunt, Dolly, going abroad, whether the quarrel was final, what Karenin would think—but not moving in with Vronsky's mother.

reading.ru: «Зачем я не умерла?» — вспомнились ей тогдашние ее слова и тогдашние ее чувства.
reading.question: What words from her past illness did Anna recall?
reading.explain: The text says she remembered her words and feelings from that time: "Why didn't I die?"

reading.ru: И стыд, и позор Алексея Александровича, и Сережи, и мой ужасный стыд, все спасается смертью!
reading.question: What did Anna believe death would save her from?
options: Shame and disgrace, for herself, Karenin, and Seryozha
reading.correct: Shame and disgrace, for herself, Karenin, and Seryozha
reading.explain: The text says she thought dying would save everyone from shame and disgrace—Karenin's, Seryozha's, and her own.

reading.ru: «Ты сам знаешь», – сказала она, и в ту же минуту, не в силах удерживаться более, она зарыдала.
reading.question: What did Anna do right after saying "You know yourself"?
reading.explain: The text says that, unable to hold back any longer, she burst into sobs.

reading.ru: Она обнимала его, покрывала поцелуями его голову, шею, руки.
reading.question: How does the chapter end?
options: With Anna embracing Vronsky and covering him with kisses
reading.correct: With Anna embracing Vronsky and covering him with kisses
reading.explain: The final sentence says she embraced him, covering his head, neck, and hands with kisses.
